title: Every Single Time
logline: When small squirrel Bo cannot make himself leave home for the Learning Circle, Keen and Aida help him discover that worry can come along too — and that the thing he wants to hide may be the thing everyone loves first.

episodeVision.premise: A nervous young squirrel tries to delay his first trip to the Learning Circle, but friendship turns his uncontrollable tail-poof from a shameful giveaway into a game that helps him step forward.
episodeVision.dramaticQuestion: Can Bo go toward a new group without first becoming someone tidier, smaller, or less visibly worried?
episodeVision.theme: Bravery is not waiting until the worry disappears; it is taking the next small step while being kindly seen.
episodeVision.externalJourney: Bo packs, unpacks, freezes at the door, meets Keen, walks through the Whispering Woods, receives Aida’s support, arrives at the Learning Circle, and ends the day laughing with a new friend.
episodeVision.internalJourney: Bo begins convinced that the visible signs of his worry will make others reject him; through Keen’s delight, Aida’s quiet truth, and the group’s welcome, he learns his tell can become connection rather than proof he does not belong.
episodeVision.relationshipChanges: Bo and Keen move from stranger-at-the-door to walking partners to laughing friends. Aida shifts from distant elder who senses his need to warm companion who admits the same hard thing. The Learning Circle changes from an imagined judging crowd into a real group that wants Bo exactly as he arrives.
episodeVision.emotionalCurve: Playful stealth opens the world; Aida’s vision introduces Bo’s stuckness; Bo’s private worry builds into a visible tail-poof; Keen’s curiosity softens it into connection; the woods let the fear return; Aida’s honesty steadies him; the Crystal Calls make the next steps feel held; the group’s delight completes the belonging; the sunset button releases the episode back into comedy with the ache intact.
episodeVision.comedyCurve: Honeycomb sneak-suspense and sneeze timing set a playful tone; Bo’s pack/unpack loop gives domestic comedy from worry; Keen’s useless tail gag reverses Bo’s embarrassment; the countdown tail-poof turns a symptom into play; Sunny’s cake-burst and Luna’s tiny brake keep the Learning Circle funny; the final Fuzzby flower-disguise crash pays off the opening honeycomb challenge.
episodeVision.setupPayoffMap: The untouched honeycomb and Fuzzby’s sleepy warning in Scene 1 pay off in the sunset garden disguise in Scene 8. Aida’s vision of Bo packing and unpacking pays off when she notices he packed four times. Bo’s conker and satchel reveal his need for something familiar to hold. The feared tail-poof becomes first Keen’s wonder, then a walking game, then the group’s delight, then Bo’s shared joke with Keen. Aida’s phrase “Every single time” becomes Bo’s carried line as he steps forward.
episodeVision.visualMotifs: Satchel-in, satchel-out; the shiny conker held close; Bo’s tail swelling from alarm to play to celebration; open door thresholds; dappled paths; pink and blue light joining on the forest floor; the honeycomb remaining untouched while schemes orbit it.
episodeVision.sonicMotifs: Fuzzby’s soft snore-bubbles and buzz-crash bookend the episode; Bo’s tail-poof becomes a friendly percussion pop; the crystal bowl’s warm G tone opens Aida’s seeing; Aida’s rose warmth and Keen’s aquamarine brightness form the emotional chord for the walk; Zenny’s om returns the world to comic stillness.
episodeVision.climax: In the forest, after Aida admits she still goes every single time, her rose-pink light and Keen’s aquamarine light join on the path, and Bo takes the first steps toward the Learning Circle while carrying the line for himself.
episodeVision.resolution: Bo is welcomed, his tail-poof becomes a game everyone enjoys, and by afternoon he can say he is glad he came. The final sunset returns to the honeycomb rivalry, showing that the day has warmed without becoming perfect or tidy.
episodeVision.intendedFinalFeeling: A small relieved laugh: the child feels Bo made friends, while the adult feels the tenderness of being allowed to arrive visibly unsure and still be welcomed.

storyTruth.falseBelief: If his worry shows, especially through his tail, the others will not like him.
storyTruth.practicalWant: To avoid the Learning Circle until he feels certain it will be okay.
storyTruth.keyRelationship: Bo and Keen, with Aida as the elder who sees and steadies the next step.
storyTruth.emotionalFearOrWound: Being new means being visibly different before anyone knows him.
storyTruth.transformedAction: Bo walks toward the Learning Circle, lets his tail-poof be seen, and joins the game instead of hiding it.
storyTruth.themeProvenThroughAction: Bo proves that belonging begins when he takes one small step while still carrying the worry, and others meet the real him with delight.

transformationMap.believes: Getting near what he wants is a game of daring and control; if caught, he can laugh and try again later.
transformationMap.does: Keen sneaks toward Fuzzby’s honeycomb, fails because of a sneeze, and walks away amused rather than crushed.
transformationMap.relationshipCondition: Keen and Fuzzby are comic rivals; Zenny watches with dry affection from the edge.
transformationMap.audienceFeeling: Sunny, giggly readiness for a small adventure.

transformationMap.believes: Someone nearby is stuck and needs help before the day can move forward.
transformationMap.feels: Aida feels quiet concern; Bo feels trapped between leaving and staying.
transformationMap.does: Aida sees Bo in her rose-lit vision packing and unpacking, then sends Keen toward him.
transformationMap.relationshipCondition: Aida is connected to Bo before he knows her; Keen becomes the bridge.
transformationMap.audienceFeeling: Curiosity with a gentle tug of concern.

transformationMap.believes: Bo believes postponing will keep him safe; Keen believes meeting him cheerfully will help.
transformationMap.feels: Bo is wound tight; Keen is open and impressed rather than judging.
transformationMap.does: Bo freezes at the door, loops the conker in and out of the bag, then startles when Keen arrives; his tail poofs and Keen calls it amazing.
transformationMap.relationshipCondition: Bo and Keen shift from strangers to a first spark of trust.
transformationMap.audienceFeeling: Recognition, laughter, and relief that the embarrassing thing is admired.

transformationMap.believes: Bo starts to believe the tail-poof can be played with, but not yet that he can face the group.
transformationMap.feels: Joy breaks through, then worry returns with a heavier truth.
transformationMap.does: Bo and Keen turn the tail-poof into a countdown game, then Bo stops and admits the real problem is being unknown by everyone at the Learning Circle.
transformationMap.relationshipCondition: Keen stops performing help and simply sits beside him with space.
transformationMap.audienceFeeling: A laugh caught by a small inhale.

transformationMap.believes: Maybe grown, confident characters never feel this before they go.
transformationMap.feels: Bo feels exposed and small; the woods go quiet around him.
transformationMap.does: Aida arrives awkwardly from the trees, sits near but not too close, and admits she would have packed five times and still goes every single time.
transformationMap.relationshipCondition: Aida becomes not an unreachable elder but a companion who knows the same doorstep.

transformationMap.believes: Bo can go with the worry, one step at a time, because he is not going alone.
transformationMap.feels: Still unsure, but held by rose and blue light.
transformationMap.does: Aida and Keen make their Crystal Calls; their lights join on the path; Bo takes a step, then another, and repeats Aida’s truth for himself.
transformationMap.relationshipCondition: The support becomes shared action, not advice; Bo, Keen, and Aida move together.

transformationMap.believes: The thing that showed his worry can also show his playfulness and help him belong.
transformationMap.feels: Open, delighted, and still tender from the cost of arriving.
transformationMap.does: Bo’s tail-poof becomes the Learning Circle’s joyful game, then he sits with Keen drawing and laughing as Aida watches with a soft glow.
transformationMap.relationshipCondition: Bo has a place in the group and a first real friend in Keen.
transformationMap.audienceFeeling: Satisfied warmth with a final comic smile.

tapestryMap.physicalMotifArc: Bo’s conker moves in and out of the satchel as a tiny anchor of control; his tail moves from uncontrollable alarm to chosen play to social celebration. Keen’s body stays forward and encouraging, but the decisive shift is that he sits beside Bo rather than pulling him.
tapestryMap.visualMotifArc: Doorways, paths, and circles carry the episode: Bo at the hollow door, the winding woods path, the glowing path after the calls, then the Learning Circle where his difference becomes central instead of hidden.
tapestryMap.colourAndLightJourney: Warm morning gold begins as playful safety; Aida’s rose vision narrows the focus to care; Bo’s hollow stays cozy but tight; the woods are dappled and uncertain; rose and aquamarine light join into an inviting path; the clearing becomes sunny and open; sunset gold closes the honeycomb joke with peace.
tapestryMap.sourceSoundArc: Crunching steps, snore-bubble pops, sneezes, satchel rustles, conker handling, tail-poof pops, leaf-and-wood knocks, group cheers, drawing-leaf scratches, and the final buzz-crash form a gentle comic sound ladder.
tapestryMap.musicMotifArc: Begin with light pizzicato mischief around Keen and Fuzzby; let Aida’s bowl introduce a sustained warm G; add small tremolo plucks around Bo’s conker loop; bring in Keen’s bright B as he reframes the tail; resolve the woods with Aida’s G and Keen’s B glowing together under soft strings; finish with sunny ensemble warmth and a tiny bee-comedy sting.
tapestryMap.environmentalMetaphor: The hollow tree is safe but circular, keeping Bo turning in place. The path through the woods lets worry walk beside him. The Learning Circle turns the feared group into a held shape. Keen’s garden at sunset shows life continuing around an untouched temptation.
tapestryMap.openingImage: Keen tiptoeing through dew-bright wildflowers toward a honeycomb while Fuzzby sleeps on top of it, danger reduced to a snore bubble.
tapestryMap.finalImage: A wide golden garden: the honeycomb still untouched, Fuzzby tangled in flower petals, and the day resting in a joke that no longer needs victory.
tapestryMap.transformedMeaning: What looked like a sign that Bo could not go becomes the very thing that lets him be known.

orderedEvents.text: Golden morning light. Dew sparkles on wildflowers. A honeycomb sits on a small stump. KEEN tiptoes toward it. He lifts his knees high with every step.
CRUNCH. CRUNCH. CRUNCH.
Keen freezes each time. He spots the honeycomb. His eyes widen. He LICKS HIS LIPS. He reaches toward the honey. FUZZBY the bee is asleep on top of the honeycomb.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
A small snore bubble grows from his nose. Keen reaches closer to the honey. POP! The bubble bursts. Keen FREEZES.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
Another bubble slowly grows. Keen inches closer to the honey.
POP! The second bubble bursts.

beats.storyBeat: Keen treats the honeycomb like a grand mission, but the world keeps making tiny betrayals: crunchy steps, Fuzzby’s sleeping body, and snore bubbles that pop at exactly the wrong moment. The beat is about the fun of wanting something before the real episode asks what it costs to go after anything.
beats.want: Keen wants to get close enough to the honeycomb without waking Fuzzby.
beats.need: He needs to learn that not every daring move is true courage; sometimes the body gives you away before you are ready.
beats.kidRead: Keen is sneaking for honey and the sleeping bee might wake up.
beats.adultRead: A child rehearses bravery in a low-stakes game, thrilled by the risk because nothing real is on the line yet.
beats.emotionalIntent: Play suspense as gentle, sunny mischief with clear anticipation and release.

beats.adultRead: The funniest part is the doomed effort to look composed while the body has already decided otherwise.
beats.emotionalIntent: Build a classic hold-and-pop gag, then let Keen’s embarrassed politeness keep it warm.

beats.need: Keen needs to feel challenged without confusing the challenge with rejection.

beats.adultRead: Fuzzby’s authority is all performance; Keen’s smile shows a healthy child can be blocked and still stay buoyant.
beats.emotionalIntent: Let the joke land in Fuzzby’s sleepy overconfidence and Keen’s amused refusal to be crushed.

beats.storyBeat: Zenny, who has quietly witnessed the whole rivalry, opens one eye and gives the smallest possible sign that she is in on the joke. Her stillness turns the scene from contest into affectionate routine.
beats.want: Zenny wants to remain undisturbed while privately enjoying the nonsense.
beats.need: The scene needs a quiet witness who tells the audience this world is safe and playful.
beats.kidRead: The calm bee saw everything and winks.
beats.adultRead: The funniest approval is the one that barely admits it is approval.
beats.emotionalIntent: End the opening on deadpan calm: one tiny wink after all that effort.

orderedEvents.text: Soft mist floats through tall trees. AIDA sits beside a crystal bowl. She slowly circles a mallet around the rim. A warm tone hums through the clearing. Her ROSE QUARTZ PENDANT begins to glow. Pink light fills her eyes.
VISION – THROUGH AIDA'S EYES
A small red squirrel sits inside a hollow tree. He packs a satchel. Unpacks it. Packs it again. He doesn't move. BACK TO SCENE. Aida gently stops the bowl. She places a paw on her heart.

beats.storyBeat: Aida’s crystal bowl shifts the episode from comic appetite to emotional seeing. In the rose-lit vision, Bo’s repeated packing and unpacking reveals a child stuck at the start line, unable to make the first move.
beats.want: Aida wants to listen closely enough to understand who needs help.
beats.need: She needs to respond with presence rather than control, trusting a gentle nudge will be enough.
beats.kidRead: Aida’s magic bowl shows a squirrel who keeps packing his bag but does not go.
beats.adultRead: The parent sees the paralysis of a child trying to prepare perfectly because leaving feels too big.
beats.emotionalIntent: Use stillness and soft mystery to make Bo’s stuckness feel important, not scary.

orderedEvents.text: Warm sunlight fills a cozy hollow tree. BO, a young red squirrel, sits beside a small satchel. Next to him lies a shiny CONKER. His Mum calls to him from offscreen, we never actually see his Mum.

orderedEvents.speaker: Bo's Mum
orderedEvents.text: BO, it’s time for you to go to the Learning Circle? Don’t forget your lunch.
Bo calls back to his Mum

orderedEvents.speaker: Bo
orderedEvents.text: I’ll go in a minute Mum.
(to the conker) Or forty. Forty sounds much better to me.

beats.storyBeat: Inside the warm hollow, Bo is surrounded by everything familiar: satchel, conker, Mum’s voice from elsewhere. He answers with delay, and his aside to the conker reveals that one minute is really a wish to postpone the whole day.
beats.want: Bo wants to stay home a little longer while appearing almost ready.
beats.need: He needs permission to begin imperfectly rather than waiting for readiness to arrive.
beats.kidRead: Bo does not want to leave yet and talks to his conker.
beats.adultRead: The ordinary domestic call exposes how huge a simple departure can feel to a child.
beats.emotionalIntent: Keep the room cozy but slightly circular, so safety also feels like being stuck.

beats.storyBeat: Bo reaches the open door and freezes. The conker and satchel become a loop of control: in, out, in, out, as his hope that today could be okay flips back into the dread that it might not.
beats.want: Bo wants to decide whether today is safe enough to face.
beats.need: He needs someone to interrupt the loop kindly, without shaming the loop.
beats.kidRead: Bo keeps putting the conker in the bag and taking it out because he cannot decide.
beats.adultRead: This is the precise physical logic of spiralling: the task is tiny, but the imagined world outside the door is enormous.
beats.emotionalIntent: Make the repetition funny at first, then let the panic quietly overtake the joke.

beats.storyBeat: Keen arrives at the doorway with a friendly knock, but his brightness startles Bo so badly the conker launches into the air. Bo’s frantic catch becomes a readable map of how tightly he is holding himself together.
beats.want: Keen wants to introduce himself and make the meeting easy; Bo wants to regain control of the conker and the moment.
beats.need: Bo needs to be met by someone who can see the fumble and not turn it into shame.
beats.kidRead: Keen says hello, Bo jumps, and the conker almost gets away.
beats.adultRead: The first meeting is not graceful, which is exactly why it can become honest.
beats.emotionalIntent: Stage the startle as slapstick with a soft landing: the conker is safe, and so is Bo.

beats.storyBeat: Bo finally says what he fears: the group may not like him, and his tail may betray him. The tail immediately does exactly that, twice, but Keen’s reaction is wonder rather than alarm, turning Bo’s worst proof into a possible gift.
beats.want: Bo wants his tail to behave normally so he can avoid being noticed for the wrong reason.
beats.need: He needs to discover that being visibly himself can invite delight rather than rejection.
beats.kidRead: Bo’s tail gets huge and fluffy, and Keen thinks it is amazing.
beats.adultRead: A child’s embarrassing tell is transformed because another child refuses to read it as embarrassing.
beats.emotionalIntent: Let the poof be big, funny, and vulnerable, then land the whole beat on Bo’s surprised hope.

cuts.action: His tail suddenly POOFS twice its size. Bo grabs it.

cuts.speaker: Bo
cuts.exactText: Stop it! Please just be a normal tail!
cuts.dialogue: Bo: Stop it! Please just be a normal tail!

cuts.action: The tail refuses. POOFS twice its size again.
Keen stares. Impressed.

cuts.speaker: Keen
cuts.dialogue: Keen: Whoa. Your tail is AMAZING.

cuts.action: Bo pauses his struggle with his tail and begins to calm down.

orderedEvents.speaker: Keen
orderedEvents.text: Mine does nothing. Watch.
Keen turns around and wiggles. His tail hangs there. Completely still.

orderedEvents.speaker: Keen
orderedEvents.text: See? Nothing.
Bo looks at Keen's tail. Then at his own. His tail slowly deflates. He almost smiles.

orderedEvents.speaker: Keen
orderedEvents.text: Let’s go for a walk and get some fresh air. Fresh air always helps.
BO’s smile grows to a full smile.

orderedEvents.speaker: Bo
orderedEvents.text: That does sound nice.
His tail deflates, picks up his bag and walks out the door with Keen.

beats.storyBeat: Keen offers his own tail as comparison and it does absolutely nothing. The anti-performance makes Bo laugh inwardly enough for his tail to soften, and the invitation to walk becomes possible because it is only a walk, not the whole feared arrival.
beats.want: Keen wants to make Bo feel less alone by showing his own tail is boring.
beats.need: Bo needs the next step made small, ordinary, and companionable.
beats.kidRead: Keen wiggles his tail but nothing happens, which makes Bo feel better.
beats.adultRead: Keen helps by lowering the stakes, not by explaining them; he makes leaving feel like a shared stroll.
beats.emotionalIntent: Use a gentle body gag to turn panic into the first full smile.

orderedEvents.text: 3,2,1 … POOF! The tail does ‘The Thing’ again and again. Bo giggles.

beats.want: Bo wants to enjoy the walk and control the tail-poof as play.
beats.need: He needs a first experience of his difference being shared safely.
beats.kidRead: They count down and Bo’s tail goes POOF again and again.
beats.adultRead: Play gives Bo temporary distance from the fear without pretending the fear is gone.
beats.emotionalIntent: Make the woods feel lighter through repetition, rhythm, and shared laughter.
